entities.summary:
Visual Basic, a groundbreaking event-driven programming language and integrated development environment (IDE) released by Microsoft in 1991 CE, fundamentally democratized software development for the Windows operating system. Conceived by Alan Cooper and later acquired and developed by Microsoft, it offered a rapid application development (RAD) paradigm that allowed programmers to visually design graphical user interfaces (GUIs) by dragging and dropping elements onto a form, then writing code behind these elements. This departure from traditional, text-based coding environments significantly lowered the barrier to entry for creating complex desktop applications, influencing countless developers globally.

The genesis of Visual Basic stemmed from a prototype named 'Ruby' by Alan Cooper, which Microsoft acquired and integrated into its QuickBasic compiler. The first version, Visual Basic 1.0, debuted at the Windows World conference in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1991, quickly gaining traction due to its intuitive visual design tools and robust backend capabilities. Subsequent versions, such as VB3 (1993) and VB6 (1998), introduced enhanced database connectivity, object-oriented features, and improved performance, cementing its status as a dominant tool for business application development. Its component object model (COM) architecture also fostered a vibrant ecosystem of third-party controls, further extending its utility and reach across industries.
